create_task.description: Create a new Asana task in a workspace, and optionally in one or more of its projects.
create_task.name: create_task

parameters.description: The title of the task, for example, Review Q3 budget.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The workspace to create the task in. Beta. Leave it out (or empty) to use the connected account's workspace when it has just one, so a workflow with several tasks doesn't ask for it each time; an account with several workspaces needs one chosen here. Leave it out too when the task goes into a project an earlier step created.
parameters.name: workspace

parameters.description: Projects to add the task to. Pick a workspace first to load its projects.
parameters.name: projects

parameters.description: The task description / notes.
parameters.name: notes

parameters.description: The workspace member to assign the task to. Pick a workspace first to load its members. A person's email address works too, such as one read from a form or a sheet. When the assignee is the same person every run (the IT contact, the HR lead), write it as "" in the workflow, so it is listed for the person to pick by name in the step, and say who it is in the step's title; don't add a setup question asking for their email. Left out altogether, the task is assigned to nobody.
parameters.name: assignee

parameters.description: The day the task is due, in YYYY-MM-DD format.
parameters.name: due_on

parameters.description: Beta. Due this many working days (Monday to Friday) after the day the step runs, for example 5 for 'due in a week'. A negative number counts back, such as -5 for 'ready 5 working days before the start date'. Use it instead of Due date when the deadline is a number of days from now or from a date, so no earlier step has to work the date out. Due date wins when both are given.
parameters.name: due_in_working_days

parameters.description: Beta. With Due in working days: count from this date instead of from the day the step runs, such as a new hire's start date, so no earlier step has to work the due date out. Leave empty to count from today.
parameters.name: working_days_from

parameters.description: Beta. Due this many calendar days (weekends included) after the day the step runs, for example 30 for a '30-day check-in', or a negative number to count back from the start date. Use it instead of Due date when the deadline is a number of days from now or from a start date, so no earlier step has to work the date out. Due date and Due in working days win when given.
parameters.name: due_in_days

parameters.description: Beta. With Due in days: count from this date instead of from the day the step runs, such as a new hire's start date. Leave empty to count from today.
parameters.name: days_from

find_completed_tasks.description: Beta. List the tasks in an Asana project that were completed in the last few days, newest first, each with who completed it, when, and its link. Its by_person groups them by who completed them (their assignee when Asana doesn't say), with their tasks written as lines, ready for a weekly 'what got done' summary with no grouping step.

find_completed_tasks.display_str_template: Find completed tasks in Asana project '{1}'.
find_completed_tasks.name: find_completed_tasks

parameters.description: The workspace the project is in; it only loads the project list.

by_person.description: The tasks grouped by who completed them, for a summary per person.

find_my_tasks.description: List your own unfinished Asana tasks across a whole workspace, with each one's due date and link. Give Due before to get only the overdue ones (today's date finds everything past due), most overdue first. Tasks with no due date are left out then.
find_my_tasks.display_str_template: Find my open tasks in Asana workspace '{1}'.
find_my_tasks.name: find_my_tasks

parameters.description: The workspace to look in.
parameters.name: workspace

parameters.description: Only tasks due before this day (YYYY-MM-DD). Use today's date for overdue tasks. Leave empty for all open tasks.
parameters.name: due_before

parameters.description: The most tasks to return (1-500, default 100).
parameters.name: limit

find_tasks.description: List the tasks in an Asana project that are not finished, each with its assignee's name and email, due date and link. Give Due before to get only the overdue ones (today's date finds everything past due), most overdue first. Tasks with no due date are left out then. Give Due on (beta) for the tasks due on one exact day, such as tomorrow. Its by_person (beta) groups the assigned tasks per person, with their tasks written as lines, ready for a message to each person.
find_tasks.display_name: Find open tasks in a project
find_tasks.display_str_template: Find open tasks in Asana project '{1}'.
find_tasks.name: find_tasks

parameters.description: The workspace the project is in; it only loads the project list.
parameters.name: workspace

parameters.description: The project to look in. Pick a workspace first to load its projects.
parameters.name: project

parameters.description: Only tasks due before this day (YYYY-MM-DD). Use today's date for overdue tasks. Leave empty for all open tasks.
parameters.name: due_before

parameters.description: Beta. Only tasks due on exactly this day (YYYY-MM-DD), such as tomorrow's date for a reminder the day before. Leave empty to ignore.
parameters.name: due_on

parameters.description: The most tasks to return (1-500, default 100).
parameters.name: limit

by_person.description: Beta. The assigned tasks grouped by person, for one message each. Unassigned tasks are left out.

count.description: How many of the tasks are theirs

output.custom_fields: (beta) The task's custom fields, each under its name as Asana shows it, with its value as text ("" when empty). Read one as a field named the way Asana shows it, such as Client email.

output.due_on: The day it is due, empty if none.
output.name: The task's name.
output.project: The ID of the project it was found in.

asana_task_completed_trigger.description: Runs when a task in an Asana project is marked complete, with its name, assignee and when it was completed.

output.assignee: Who it is assigned to: name, email, gid. Empty if nobody.
output.completed_date: (beta) The day it was marked complete, such as 2026-11-14, for a sheet or a date field (the day in UTC).
output.completed_display: (beta) The day it was marked complete, written for a message, such as November 14, 2026 (the day in UTC).
output.custom_fields: (beta) The task's custom fields, each under its name as Asana shows it, with its value as text ("" when empty). Read one as a field named the way Asana shows it, such as Client email.
output.due_on: The day it is due, empty if none.
output.name: The task's name.
output.project: The ID of the project it was found in.

parameters.description: The workspace the project is in, to pick the project from a list.
